claims.statement: Casbin uses a deny-override policy model with keyMatch2 URL matching and * HTTP method wildcard; a new endpoint without a policy row is denied by default (safe by construction).

Roles are admin (full wildcard), partner (project-scoped with explicit deny on bulk-approve, bulk-reject, reset), adv_partner (import, view/export, no financial actions), and employee (self-service /api/v1/me/* plus employee-mobile flows); notifications and push subscription endpoints are open to any authenticated role.

Partner scoping requires both Casbin (endpoint-level allow/deny) and handler-level checks via isScopedPartnerRole + CanUserAccessProject / CanUserAccessEmployee; the second layer is required because Casbin cannot decide which rows within an endpoint the partner can see.

The password-reset request endpoint always returns 200 (anti-enumeration) and is rate-limited 3/hr per normalized email; the confirm flow atomically consumes the Redis token via GETDEL, updates the password, and invalidates every existing session (tokens_invalid_before) in a single DB transaction. Mounted only when PASSWORD_RESET_ENABLE=true.
Adding a new role or changing permissions is a CSV edit (backend/configs/casbin_policy.csv); no Go code change required.

The audit middleware sets actor_id, request_id, and ip on the per-request audit context; the non-blocking emit pattern is go func() { _ = auditService.LogXxx(ctx, ...) }() and always includes data_type, record_count, file_name for imports/exports.
